newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan new-crop cotton rates up on mill demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan new-crop cotton rates up on mill demand.

text.p: Pakistan's new-crop cotton rates gained on Tuesday on demand from mills and could rise more because of slow arrival of fresh supplies, dealers said.
"There is a good demand from mills which exceeds supply," dealer Khushi Ram said. "The prices will gain further as supplies from Punjab province will come in full swing not before mid-September."
In the kerb market, the new-crop (1997/98) NIAB-78 variety was quoted between 2,265 ($55.76) and 2,270 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
